description: CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became (util.DateUtilityJob) and never through a JobLauncher or an HTTP layer: no EXEC PGM= anywhere in app/jcl or app/proc names it, and it is CALLed four times from two online programs - CORPT00C at L392 and L412, COTRN02C at L393 and L413. LS-DATE='0000-01-01' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='YYYY-MM-DD' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85), each written out to the declared PIC X(10) width; LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the entire output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. The program declares no ENVIRONMENT DIVISION, no SELECT and no FD, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and leaves no final state to state; it also declares no job parameter, and not merely because no JCL reaches it - ParityCase refuses a job parameter on any unitKind but BATCH_JOB, since an input member holding a value the case also expects would be fed back into the unit and then compared against itself. Its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. This case pins arm 9 of the ten-arm EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149: FC-YEAR-IN-ERA-ZERO, 88-level VALUE X'000309D959C3C5C5' (L70), the last of the nine NAMED arms. Both numbers in the message are DECODED from that hex rather than interpolated from the neighbouring arms - the leading halfword 0x0003 is the severity, which L123 renders '0003' through the WS-SEVERITY-N PIC 9(4) REDEFINES at L44 and L98 moves to RETURN-CODE as 3, and the second halfword 0x09D9 is message 2521, which L124 renders '2521' through the WS-MSG-NO-N REDEFINES at L47. The trailing 59 C3 C5 C5 is the condition's CASE-SEV-CTL severity-control byte (L78) and its FACILITY-ID (L79), and those last three bytes spell 'CEE' only when read as EBCDIC, never as ASCII; they take no part in the message, whose own bytes are compared under US-ASCII. The fifteen characters at offset 20 are WS-RESULT PIC X(15) (L49), and the arm literal at L146 already fills it exactly, so nothing pads it. What the case pins is a year within the era of zero, which no era admits: the count begins at one on both sides of the epoch, so there is no year zero to convert. The precedence is the reason this case exists rather than merely the value. The year is examined before the epoch range, so '0000-01-01' reports 2521 and NOT the 2513 FC-UNSUPP-RANGE that a date preceding the Lillian epoch would otherwise attract - in an ordered guard chain the first failure wins, which makes the order of the checks part of the contract and not an implementation detail. It is also not 2518, because the picture string 'YYYY-MM-DD' parses, and not 2520, because every numeric position holds a digit; a validator that ranged the date first, or that read four zero digits as an absent year and defaulted it, would report one of those instead, and this case is what holds it to 2521. WS-DATE at offset 45 then reports two binary bytes ahead of only the first eight characters of the date: L105-L106 takes LENGTH OF LS-DATE - the DECLARED length, hence always 10, never the length of any value - into VSTRING-LENGTH, and the GROUP move at L122 overwrites the clean copy made at L107-L108 with the leftmost ten bytes of WS-DATE-TO-TEST, which are that Vstring-length halfword X'000A' followed by '0000-01-' alone, the final '01' falling outside the ten. That corruption is expected output and is preserved rather than corrected. WS-DATE-FMT at offset 66 is by contrast clean, because L111-L113 set it by an ordinary X(10) to X(10) move before the CALL and L122 targets WS-DATE alone. The line is eighty bytes wide whatever the input was, and the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 is summed span by span to prove it: 4 + 11 + 4 + 1 + 15 + 1 + 9 + 10 + 1 + 10 + 10 + 1 + 3 = 80, with 'Mesg Code:' ten characters inside a PIC X(11) span and 'TstDate:' eight inside a PIC X(09), each right-padded by its own VALUE clause, while 'Mask used:' exactly fills its PIC X(10) and needs no pad; INITIALIZE at L90 does not clear a FILLER, so all three literals survive. On the tenth arm, because this file is the twentieth and last of the set: WHEN OTHER at L147-L148 moves 'Date is invalid' into that same WS-RESULT - already exactly fifteen characters, and not to be confused with arm 1's 'Date is valid', thirteen plus two of pad and carrying the opposite meaning and a RETURN-CODE of 0 - and it must remain LAST, since EVALUATE TRUE takes the first matching WHEN and this arm is the default. It has no 88-level VALUE of its own and no pair of inputs can select it, because this translation reproduces CEEDAYS as a total guard chain and never manufactures an unenumerated token. The nine enumerated message numbers are 0 for the all-zeros success token at L62 and then 2507, 2508, 2509, 2513, 2517, 2518, 2520 and 2521, a NON-CONTIGUOUS set whose gaps are 2510, 2511, 2512, 2514, 2515, 2516 and 2519; so a structurally genuine feedback token - the same 0x0003 severity, the same 0x59 control byte and the same EBCDIC 'CEE' facility every named error carries - still falls through to arm 10 whenever its message halfword lands in that gap, X'000309D259C3C5C5' at 2514 sitting immediately AFTER the recognised 2513 and X'000309D759C3C5C5' at 2519 immediately BEFORE the recognised 2520, fencing both edges of the largest gap region against any implementation that assumed the numbers ran consecutively. Arm 10 is therefore exercised where its mapping actually lives - by DateUtilityJobTest through the package-private resultTextOfFeedbackToken seam in com.vsergeychik.carddemo.util - rather than from a parity case, which has no member able to carry a raw token and would have to assert its own decode straight back out. Across case01 to case20 all nine REACHABLE arms are covered and this file is the sole carrier of arm 9. Expected values here are STATICALLY DERIVED by structured reading of app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl - the WS-MESSAGE spans at L42-L57, the nine tokens at L62-L70, the arm literal at L146, the group move at L122 and the EVALUATE at L128-L149 - and were NOT captured from any execution of the COBOL, which is impossible in this environment: PROCEDURE DIVISION USING at L88 makes this a subprogram the available compiler refuses to build as an executable, and cobc --list-intrinsics matches zero CEE* entries, so the CALL "CEEDAYS" at L116 that decides every outcome has no implementation to call. Only the provenance of the expectation is substituted; the twenty-case set, the field-by-field diff and the diff-count-of-zero gate all stand.
